scope: Release G2 of the graphics plan (docs/graphics-tripo-plan.md): arms and standards

authorization.source: docs/graphics-tripo-plan.md: release G2, capped at 700 credits on 8 November 2026, with 725 of G3’s and G5’s held credits and 420 of G4’s (#103) proposed for it, 1,845 in all; decision 9 (9 November 2026) leaves the rest of the plan to my judgement within each release’s cap, each pilot reviewed in the game before the rest of its release is generated; decision 10 puts the standards first

pricing.source: the calibration's measured prices (docs/graphics-calibration.md), and image-to-model at standard textures as G6's pilot measured it (30 credits, not the 20 the pilot planned); each task's reported credits_consumed is recorded below

paused.reason: The plan’s stop rule: 1 of the release’s 4 generations was rejected at review (g2-aquila, grey all over), over its 20%
paused.until: the owner decides whether G2 goes on (docs/graphics-tripo-plan.md, decision 13)

batches.note: G2's pilot, the standards first: a century's signum and a legion's eagle, worn on the figure's standard joint in place of the code-built pole and its ornaments, and a vexillum for the finale's blocks, each generated at standard texture and geometry (20 credits), within a 100-credit ceiling. The first eagle was rejected and redone: 80 credits.

balance.source: the account balance read before the batch’s first task and after its last (frozen 0)

tasks.rejectedAtReview: the eagle and its pole came out grey all over: a flat colour map with almost no colour in it (mean saturation 3 of 255), not the gilded eagle and dark wooden shaft asked for, the failure of G5's first ballista

rejected.note: The first eagle came out grey all over (a flat colour map with almost no colour in it (mean saturation 3 of 255), not the gilded eagle and dark wooden shaft asked for, the failure of G5's first ballista). The second, g2-aquila-b, with its colours named outright, ships as kit-aquila. One of four generations (25%), over the plan's 20% stop rule: G2 pauses after its pilot.
